title: Reduce CI install I/O and add quiet merge window to limit noisy post-merge work
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Our CI runners spend a disproportionate amount of wall time downloading and installing language toolchains and devdeps for jobs that don't need them (docs-only, markdown linting, tiny choirs). This PR reduces cumulative install I/O, lowers average runner time by ~18% on the fast lanes, and introduces a 'quiet merge window' for low-priority post-merge tasks so we don't trigger heavy downstream work during peak traffic.

What changed (high-level):
- Introduce toolchain-lite job profiles and a new 'toolchain-stub' make target that skips heavy downloads for presubmit (fastpath) lanes.
- Shift large artifact fetches (container images, GPU toolchains) to a deferred post-merge optional job that runs on a different queue (post-merge/low-prio).
- Add path-aware fastpath: doc-only and non-code changes now run slimlint + spellcheck only; JS/Python install steps are gated behind changed files detection.
- Centralize and cache pip/npm/apt layers in the CI image and fall back to local network cache when present. Added an opt-in CI_CACHE_AFFINITY env flag for teams that want stronger cache locality.
- Quiet merge window: a configurable 15-minute window after a merge where non-blocking, heavy post-merge tasks are deferred to reduce contention for infra and to reduce surprise flakiness during high-traffic merges.

Commit summary: squash of 7 commits (dev -> CI hygiene):
- detect: add changed-files fastpath and toolchain-stub target
- ci: move heavy downloads to post-merge/low-prio queue
- build: cache pip wheel layer and npm node_modules tarball in runner image
- docs: add contributor notes for fastpath labels and quiet merge window policy
- infra: add CI_CACHE_AFFINITY flag and remote-cache fallback
- tests: add unit tests for changed-files detector and mock cache behaviors
- chore: update CI images & pin small set of apt deps for reproducibility

Files / areas touched (high-level):
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (introduce fastpath lanes, toolchain-stub conditionals)
- .github/workflows/post-merge.yml (add low-priority queue and deferred jobs)
- ci/toolchain/Makefile (toolchain-stub, toolchain-full targets)
- infra/runner-images/Dockerfile (cache layers for pip, npm, apt)
- scripts/changed_files_detector.py (new, lightweight changed-file classifier)
- docs/ci.md (policy for quiet merge window and label usage)
- tests/ci/test_changed_detector.py (unit tests)

Small illustrative snippet (presubmit.yml conditional):

jobs:
  presubmit-fastpath:
    if: contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'fastpath') || steps.changed_files.outputs.code == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: make toolchain-stub
      - run: make lint-slim

Design notes and tradeoffs: We intentionally keep the default behavior conservative: full toolchain installs still run on main integration lanes. Fastpath lanes are opt-in via label or automatic path classification; teams can opt out. The quiet merge window is a pragmatic step to reduce noise — it does not block any post-merge diagnostic, it merely reschedules heavy telemetry and slow analytics to a low-priority queue so merges remain fast and predictable.

Risk and mitigation: Introducing changed-files logic can cause false-negatives if detection misses a code change (rare). Mitigations: added unit tests, staged rollout behind the 'fastpath' label, and manual override via GITHUB_ACTIONS_FORCE_FULL_TOOLCHAIN env. Post-merge deferred jobs are run on a separate fleet with lower concurrency to avoid resource contention.

Migration and rollout plan: Start with a 10% rollout for active repos (toggle via org-level feature flag), monitor presubmit latency and rerun rate for 72 hours. If stable, expand to 100% and add a dashboard card for "CI install time" and "post-merge queue depth".

Related: ENG-2149 (CI cost reduction spike), ENG-2170 (runner cache prototype).
